question:
I created a dbt macro is_date_format.sql that checks if a source_value resembles a simple date format yyyy-mm-dd (more specifically i compare the source_value to a regex pattern):

{% macro is_date_format(source_value) %}
    
    regexp_instr('{{source_value}}', '^[0-9]{4}\\-[0-9]{2}\\-[0-9]{2}$') > 0

{% endmacro %}

I am calling this macro in an if-else-statement:

{% if is_date_format(source_value) %}

    true

{% else %}

    false

{% endif %}

Somehow, this does not seem to work, because even if I am using a simple string (e.g. 'hello_world') the if-else-statement always ends up with true. The regex pattern works when testing it isolated. Only when I am using an if-else-statement this seems to be broken.

Can someone help me with that?

Thank you! :)
title: Using dbt macro in if else statement
answer: %Macro cast_date(column_name, curr_pattern)%. Cast (column_name) as date format '(curr_pattern) end macro. Then you call inside you code example : select cast_date (column_name, 'DD/MM/YYYY') fromtable
